text:
lucy-sre: Heads up — seeing a sudden burst of high-cardinality GPU metrics being scraped and forwarded to remote_write, Cortex is returning 504s. Spike started around 10:12 UTC. Anyone on this?

sam-gpuops: Yup, alerts came in for remote_write error rate + grafana panel shows a big sample-rate jump: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd/gpu-metrics?from=now-1h&to=now

nora-eng: Is this from the node exporter or the DCGM exporter? Could be batch jobs pushing to pushgateway.

sam-gpuops: Digging — prometheus scrape targets show a lot of pushgateway endpoints in prod-gpu; many short-lived jobs push per-process metrics (pid, thread_id, container_id). That exploded label cardinality.

lucy-sre: Logs from one pushgateway pod: 
```
level=info ts=2026-03-15T10:12:30Z msg="push: receive metrics" job=worker-224 instance=10.2.4.12
level=warn ts=2026-03-15T10:12:31Z msg="evicting metrics due to ttl" job=worker-224
level=error ts=2026-03-15T10:12:32Z msg="write to remote_write failed" err="504 Gateway Timeout"
```

maya-eng: Dev note: batch workers are instrumented to push per-job metrics for debugging. Shouldn't send pid/container_id to prometheus.

ben-sre: Quick mitigation: we can add metric_relabel_configs on the pushgateway scrape job to drop those high-card labels before ingestion. Example we can apply now: 
```
- job_name: 'pushgateway'
  static_configs:
    - targets: ['pushgateway.prod:9091']
  metric_relabel_configs:
    - regex: '.*'
      action: replace
      replacement: '$1'
    - source_labels: ['pid']
      action: labeldrop
    - source_labels: ['container_id', 'thread_id']
      action: labeldrop
```
(we'll tighten the first rule to only affect the specific metrics)

lucy-sre: I pushed a drop rule for pid and container_id to the prometheus scrape config and reloaded on all scrape instances. Cardiniality graph shows a ~88% drop in unique series within 4–5 minutes.

deploy-bot: prometheus-config-reloader: config updated for job=pushgateway by lucy-sre, reloaded 6 targets :white_check_mark: 

devops-bot: alert: remote_write_error_rate fired -> now 12.3% (was 21%).

nora-eng: We still see occasional remote_write timeouts — let's tune remote_write queue config as a short-term band-aid. Suggested params: 
```
remote_write:
  - url: https://cortex.prod.redwood/api/prom/push
    timeout: 30s
    queue_config:
      max_samples_per_send: 500
      batch_send_deadline: 5s
      capacity: 25000
```
Apply narrower sends so retries don't pile up.

sam-gpuops: Also adding a recording rule to aggregate per-gpu temp metrics to per-pod averages will stop us from sending raw per-process temps. Example recording rule: 
```
- record: gpu:temperature:avg
  expr: avg by(pod, gpu_index) (dcgm_gpu_temp_celsius)
  labels:
    summary: "pod-level avg"
```
That will keep useful signals but collapse cardinality.

lucy-sre: Applied metric relabel + recording rules on the test prom cluster. Aggregation rule looks good locally. Rolling to canary now.

ben-sre: FYI cost impact: that spike added ~2.1M extra samples to remote_write in the last hour -> rough egress/ingestion delta ~$120/day if sustained. We should add a guard for pushgateway to enforce TTL or stricter label whitelists.

maya-eng: Plan for follow-up: 1) enforce label whitelist on pushgateway scrape (drop unexpected labels), 2) instrument batch workers to avoid pushing debug-level per-process metrics, 3) shorten pushgateway retention TTL to 1h (was 5m causing lots of churn), 4) add alert for unique_series_rate delta.

lucy-sre: Kicking off an ops ticket and putting on incident board. I'll hand to oncall rotation to confirm stability over next 2 hours.

deploy-bot: Prometheus reload command run: `kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart statefulset/prometheus` (canary) :gear:

sam-gpuops: After relabel + queue tuning, remote_write error rate down to 0.9% and unique_series is back to baseline. Nice work :thumbsup:

lucy-sre: Closing thread — will follow up in runbook with exact relabel rules and recording rule snippets. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
